methods.label: Factor and use zero products
methods.explanation: Factoring using the cross method gives \((2x+1)(x-3)=0\), so \(x=-1/2\) or \(x=3\).
methods.levelReason: The cross factorization and zero-product rule are within Grade 9; solving the linear factors uses Grade 7 algebra.

methods.label: Use the quadratic formula
methods.explanation:
The quadratic formula uses the coefficients directly. Here \(a=2\), \(b=-5\), and \(c=-3\), so
\[
b^2-4ac=(-5)^2-4(2)(-3)=49>0.
\]
Since \(a=2\ne0\), the formula gives both real roots:
\[
x=\frac{-b\pm\sqrt{b^2-4ac}}{2a}
=\frac{5\pm7}{4}.
\]
Thus the roots are \(3,-\frac12\).
methods.levelReason: The quadratic formula is another standard Grade 9 method. Its supporting work is identifying coefficients, finding the square roots of 49, and rational arithmetic.
